newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Salinas to leave Dow Jones board - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Salinas to leave Dow Jones board - paper.

text.p: Former Mexican President Carlos Salinas de Gortari will leave the board of directors of Dow Jones & Co in April, the Mexico City newspaper El Universal reported on Friday.

Salinas, in self-imposed exile in Ireland, has been called to testify in the investigation into the 1994 assassination of Luis Donaldo Colosio, Salinas's hand-picked successor who was gunned down at a campaign rally.
Salinas answered 12 hours of questioning from a special prosecutor at the Mexican embassy in Dublin on Wednesday and will be called again next week, the Mexican government said.
Salinas denied he had any role in the Colosio murder in a letter to prosecutors that was made public on Thursday.
El Universal, citing sources "close to" Salinas in Dublin, said he would step down from Dow Jones two years after being elected to the board.
In New York, a Dow Jones spokesman said he was unaware if Salinas had told company officials he would leave the board in April, when his two-year term is up.

"I have no idea what communication may have passed between the chairman and Salinas," company spokesman Roger May said. "The only time we would say if someone is running or not running for the board of directors is when we issue our proxy statement in mid-March."

Dow Jones said Salinas was named to its board in January 1995 and "overwhelmingly" elected to a two-year term in April 1995. The former Mexican president was chosen for his global experience, the company said.

Salinas left Mexico in disgrace in March 1995 after his elder brother Raul was arrested on murder charges in a separate case. Raul Salinas is in a high security Mexican jail charged with corruption and for masterminding the murder of top Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) politician Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu.
